steps.question: Do the counts and metadata confirm 5 subjects each with one control and one treated sample, and what filtering is needed before paired differential expression?
acceptance_criteria: Metadata parsed to confirm 10 samples = 5 subjects x 2 conditions (control, treated), matched 1:1
Counts matrix (12000 genes x 10 samples) column names matched to metadata sample IDs, order verified
Low-count genes filtered (e.g., require minimum count sum or CPM threshold across samples) before DE, with number of genes retained reported
Library size / sequencing depth per sample reported to flag any outlier sample

steps.name: Paired DESeq2 differential expression (control vs treated, blocked on subject)
caveats: n=5 paired subjects is a small sample size — interpret nominal p-values cautiously and report that power is limited

steps.question: Which genes are significantly differentially expressed between treated and control samples, accounting for paired subject structure (design ~subject + condition)?
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 run with design formula ~subject + condition on the filtered count matrix from T1S1
Results table reports log2FoldChange, p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value (padj) for all tested genes, ranked by significance
Significant genes reported at padj < 0.05 (and noted if using a relaxed threshold given n=5 pairs limits power)
MA plot and/or volcano plot produced summarizing the treated vs control contrast
Sample-to-sample correlation or PCA on variance-stabilized counts reported to confirm subject pairing structure (samples from same subject cluster together prior to condition effect)

steps.name: Per-subject treated-vs-control fold changes and consistency across subjects
caveats: Per-subject fold changes from a single pair (n=1 per subject) have no within-subject variance estimate — treat these as descriptive/exploratory, not as independent significance tests
Do not present per-subject consistency counts as a formal statistical test; this step is descriptive heterogeneity characterization to complement the T1S2 population-level test
steps.question: For each of the 5 subjects individually, which genes show a treated-vs-control change, and how consistent is the direction of change across all 5 subjects (i.e., which genes respond to treatment within each subject rather than only on population average)?
acceptance_criteria: Per-subject log2 fold change (treated vs control) computed from DESeq2 size-factor-normalized (or variance-stabilized) counts for each of the 5 subjects independently
A per-gene table reporting the 5 per-subject fold changes side by side, plus the number of subjects showing concordant direction of change
Genes flagged as 'consistent responders' (same direction of change in all or a majority, e.g. >=4/5, of subjects) versus genes driven by a single subject
Cross-reference of the consistent-responder gene set against the paired DESeq2 significant gene list from T1S2 to show overlap

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of treatment-responsive genes
caveats: Confirm the human WikiPathways gene set reference file is present before running; if absent, report the gap rather than substituting a non-human or fabricated gene set
12000 background genes is a reduced universe (not whole-genome) since this appears to be a curated/targeted panel — set the ORA background accordingly to avoid inflated significance
steps.question: Which biological pathways are enriched among genes significantly differentially expressed between treated and control blood samples (from the paired DESeq2 model in T1S2)?
acceptance_criteria: Over-representation analysis run on the significant gene list (padj < 0.05, or the consistent-responder set from T1S3 if the DESeq2 list is small) against a human pathway gene set collection
Background/universe set to all genes tested in T1S2 (post-filtering), not the whole genome
Enriched pathways reported with adjusted p-values, gene counts, and the specific member genes from the input list driving each pathway
If no pathways reach significance, this is reported explicitly rather than relaxing thresholds silently

plan.title: Paired control-vs-treated DE in blood (n=5 subjects)
plan.analytical_narrative: The data context describes a paired bulk RNA-seq design: 5 subjects, each contributing a control and a treated blood sample (10 samples, 12000 genes, raw STAR/featureCounts counts). The research question — which genes respond to treatment within each subject — is a within-subject paired comparison, which requires modeling subject as a blocking factor to remove inter-subject variability and isolate the treatment effect (paired design, not independent groups). Step 1 loads and QCs the counts/metadata, confirming the paired structure (5 subjects x 2 conditions) and filtering low-count genes. Step 2 runs DESeq2 with a paired design formula (~subject + condition) to get the population-level (average within-subject) treatment effect, which directly answers 'which genes respond to treatment' in a design-appropriate way. Because the question also asks about response 'within each subject', Step 3 computes per-subject log2 fold changes (treated vs control per subject, from normalized counts) to characterize subject-level heterogeneity in response beyond the average effect, and flags genes with a consistent direction across all 5 subjects vs those driven by one outlier subject. Step 4 takes the paired DESeq2 significant gene list and runs pathway over-representation enrichment against a human pathway gene set to give biological context to the treatment response. All steps operate on the actual 12000x11 counts.csv and 10x3 metadata.csv files, using the paired design explicit in the data profile.
